name: Kupalaŭcy (Free Kupala Theatre in exile)
funding: Ticket sales; Polish Ministry of Culture (Culture Promotion Fund honorary award, 17 Mar 2025); EU ArtPower Belarus project grants; diaspora crowdfunding and guest co-productions with Polish theatres; funds for two projects via Pavel Latushka's foundation; Polish Theatre Institute residencies ended in 2024
watch: Troupe formed 6 Oct 2020 after the Janka Kupala National Theatre's company resigned en masse in Aug 2020; moved via Ukraine to Poland (Warsaw and Lublin). Actors earn about PLN 500 a show and the troupe describes its financing as near zero. Belarus declared its YouTube channel 'extremist material' in Feb 2024 and the troupe an 'extremist formation' on 13 Dec 2024; actors face warrants limiting travel.
records_note: The troupe has no website of its own, only social media and press coverage, so it publishes no reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: KX Space / Kryly Khalopa Theatre (Prastora KX, closed 2021)
funding: Independent theatre (founded 2001) running its own venue; art-sale auctions for the BYSOL solidarity fund reported; grant sources not published
watch: Independent venue opened Nov 2014 at Khalturina 2/1 (theatre, gallery, education, community events); director Aksana Haiko. The theatre still produces (2025 'Brest HERstory' audio-walk about women in Brest 1939–45) but its site gives no current base.
records_note: The theatre's site lists productions and one past partner but posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: La Casa Encendida
watch: Social and cultural center in Lavapiés run by a non-profit foundation, with programmes in avant-garde culture, ecology and solidarity.

name: La Friche la Belle de Mai
funding: Ville de Marseille, Ministère de la Culture, Région Sud, European Regional Development Fund; cooperative non-profit governance (SCIC).

name: La Station
funding: Ville de Nice, DRAC PACA (Ministère de la Culture), Région Sud; artist-run non-profit association.
watch: Artist-run space founded in 1996 in the former municipal refrigerated slaughterhouses (Les Abattoirs). Wholly self-managed by artists.

name: La Virreina Centre de la Imatge
funding: Ajuntament de Barcelona (Barcelona City Council Institute of Culture - ICUB).
watch: Public visual culture centre in an 18th-century Baroque palace on La Rambla. Directed by writer and curator Valentín Roma, it treats the image as a tool of political critique and working-class emancipation.

name: LABoral Centro de Arte y Creación Industrial
funding: Public foundation (budget about €1.3M in 2014) governed by Asturias, Gijón city and the Gijón Port Authority. Project sponsors in 2023 included the Onassis Foundation's Ariona Hellas.
watch: Housed in the Universidad Laboral building. Fundación EDP, an energy group's foundation, co-funded the Eco-Visionarios exhibition in 2018–19.
records_note: LABoral posts activity reports for 2018 to 2025, audited accounts for 2014 to 2025 and its trustees, but no list of named funders.

name: Lagos Biennial
funding: Small artist-run biennial (2024 edition; 2026 announced) by Àkéte Art Foundation; funded by Terra, Ford and Rockefeller Brothers Fund.
watch: Artist-founded biennial led by Folakunle Oshun. Its 4th edition, 2024, ran in Tafawa Balewa Square.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; the supporters page shows about 40 logos, mostly without alt text, and the site names six advisory board members.

name: Lahore Biennale Foundation
funding: Punjab and federal government bodies; lead sponsor Habib Bank; star sponsors Barjeel Art Foundation, Bareeze and ICCI; partners include Nishat, PIA, Dulux and Careem.
watch: The sponsor page is undated and shows logos only.
records_note: Its Financials page posts reports 2015 to 2025 and statements 2015 to 2024, its Board page lists the board, and sponsors appear as logos.

name: LE 18, Derb el Ferrane
funding: Artist-run space founded 2013; documenta fifteen lumbung member; funders not published.
records_note: Its About page names structural patron NOMAD (2015 to now) and partners for 2013 to 2023; no annual report, accounts or board.

name: Le 19, Crac
funding: French state (DRAC Bourgogne-Franche-Comté), Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, City of Montbéliard and Pays de Montbéliard Agglomération.
watch: Public money only; no censorship or protest found.
records_note: Names its four public funders in its About text; publishes no annual reports, accounts, private sponsors or board list.

name: Le 32Bis
funding: Private initiative opened Feb 2022 in the former Philips HQ; funded by Tunisian private patrons who are not named; partners include the African Culture Fund.
watch: 4,000 m² centre with residencies, exhibitions and a library in downtown Tunis; opened Feb 2022.
records_note: 32bis.org lists no annual reports, accounts, partners, funders, board or team.
